claims.claim: The successful mathematics used by this project is Stijn Cambie's 2024 solution of Erdős Problem #678.
claims.limitation: This does not attribute the project's Lean implementation to Cambie.

claims.claim: The repository contains an independently structured Lean reimplementation of Cambie's proof, not an independent new mathematical proof.
claims.limitation: No genealogical-independence claim beyond the recorded reconstruction process.

claims.claim: The machine-checked endpoint gives witnesses for arbitrarily large block length k and proves infinitely many good lengths.
claims.limitation: Use the exact indexing and domain conditions stated in the theorem.

claims.claim: The repository's length-based interval definition is formally bridged to the public Finset.Ioc statement convention.
claims.limitation: This is a statement-semantics bridge, not a claim that the proof implementations are identical.

claims.claim: The final #678 formalization was integrated only after canonical import-graph and full-build verification, followed by exact-main post-merge verification.
claims.limitation: Run and commit identities must be cited when making exact historical verification claims.

claims.claim: A controlled common-environment differential verification was executed against the pinned Aristotle/Boris Alexeev public formal artifact.
claims.limitation: Differential verification does not establish mathematical novelty or proof genealogy.

claims.claim: Observed dependency-surface counts are ownership- and packaging-boundary sensitive.
claims.limitation: Raw counts are not a proof-complexity or architecture-quality ranking.

claims.claim: In six credited paired runs there was no stable wall-clock winner, while CPU and memory profiles differed materially in the pinned common environment.
claims.limitation: No universal speed or maintainability claim.

claims.claim: The frozen S2c repair-locality experiment produced a mixed, interface-dependent result with no uniform winner.
claims.scope: three frozen API-reference mutations across two artifacts

claims.claim: All six credited observations from three frozen semantic/index perturbations across two artifacts were rejected; zero semantic survivors and zero proof repairs were recorded.
claims.scope: the frozen S2d perturbation set only

claims.claim: For the two exact frozen forward-version candidates, failure occurred at dependency/package boundaries before an eligible project-owned repair surface was reached.
claims.scope: U1 and U2 exact frozen candidates only
claims.limitation: No general Lean/Mathlib compatibility, future repair-cost, or maintainability conclusion.

claims.claim: In this case study, computational success was not sufficient for scientific credit when required provenance, classification, or aggregation controls were defective.
claims.limitation: The broader causal value of individual governance controls remains a hypothesis.

claims.claim: Externalized state, negative regressions, and explicit interfaces improve restart reliability and reduce repeated failure in long-horizon AI-assisted formalization.
claims.limitation: No causal comparison was prospectively designed to establish this claim.

claims.claim: This project produced a new mathematical solution or new independent mathematical proof of Erdős #678.
This project produced the first Lean formalization of Erdős #678.
claims.limitation: A prior public Aristotle/Boris Alexeev artifact is recorded.

claims.claim: The internal proof architecture is generally faster, more maintainable, more robust, or superior to alternatives.
claims.limitation: S2 results are bounded, mixed, and ownership/environment sensitive.
